title: Development and validation of artificial intelligence-based methods for detecting extracapsular extension of prostate cancer using transrectal micro-ultrasound
summary:
This is a retrospective single-center diagnostic study investigating the potential of artificial intelligence for the detection of extracapsular extension (ECE) in patients with prostate cancer using transrectal micro-ultrasound (microUS). 
Depending on the AI approach or model, different reference standards may be applied. Histopathological evaluation of radical prostatectomy specimens represents the preferred ground truth for local tumor staging and extracapsular extension, whereas histopathological biopsy findings may be used as the reference standard for other AI models or study objectives.
For example, histopathological whole-mount prostatectomy specimens serve as the reference standard for determining pathological tumor stage and the presence or absence of extracapsular extension.
MicroUS images will be retrospectively correlated with the corresponding histopathological findings using anatomical landmarks. Tumor regions will be annotated based on histopathological reference labels, resulting in a structured and histopathologically validated imaging dataset. This dataset will be used for the development, training, and validation of different AI-based classification models for automated differentiation between organ-confined (pT2) and locally advanced (pT3) prostate cancer.
The diagnostic performance of the developed models will be assessed on independent validation and test datasets using established diagnostic accuracy metrics, including the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, and overall accuracy. The study aims to evaluate the potential of AI-assisted micro-ultrasound image analysis to improve the preoperative detection of extracapsular extension and to support surgical decision-making.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Preoperative transrectal micro-ultrasound examination with digitally stored image data or histopathological biopsy results.
Exclusion criteria:
Insufficient micro-ultrasound image quality preventing reliable annotation or AI analysis.
Incomplete clinical, imaging, or histopathological data.
No written formal consent.
